records.rationale: The masked randomized comparison directly informs this symptom-recovery endpoint, and the credible interval is close to no effect. Postrandomization drug-delivery exclusions, participant-reported recovery, a skeptical Bayesian prior and the selected Omicron-era population leave uncertainty about smaller effects and applicability; the result is informative without proving equivalence.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Random allocation and matching placebo reduce confounding; the prespecified modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded 33 randomized participants without timely drug delivery, and recovery was reported remotely by participants.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: This is direct evidence for 13 days of higher-dose fluvoxamine during early acute COVID-19 in adults at least 30 years old; it is not treatment evidence for established Long COVID.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The adjusted recovery HR of 0.99 has a 95% Bayesian credible interval of 0.89–1.09; the prespecified efficacy probability threshold was not met. Smaller differences remain possible.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: This exact dose, population and recovery definition are represented by one selected report. Other doses and COVID-OUT’s severe-event composite are separate questions rather than interchangeable replication.

records.rationale: The randomized masked factorial comparison directly evaluates fluvoxamine for this 14-day composite and controls for concurrent co-treatment assignments. However, an imprecise odds-ratio interval, home-oximetry ascertainment, modified intention-to-treat exclusions and limited population scope prevent high confidence in a precise effect size. Benefit was not demonstrated, and equivalence was not established.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Site-stratified random allocation, matching pills and concurrent controls support a causal comparison. The prespecified modified intention-to-treat set excluded participants not receiving study drug; primary missingness was 1.4% and imputed.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The report directly studies fluvoxamine at 50 mg twice daily for 14 days in early acute COVID-19 with overweight or obesity. Its mixed hypoxemia/health-care endpoint is distinct from sustained recovery or later Long COVID.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The adjusted odds ratio 0.94 (95% CI 0.66–1.36) spans lower and higher odds. Rare hospitalizations and deaths are not precisely estimated by this composite result.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: Only one exact report and drug-specific comparison are assessed here. Other arms in the same factorial trial are not independent replications; no cross-drug pooling or between-arm marginal-rate comparison is valid.

records.rationale: The masked randomized design directly addresses visceral adiposity at 48 weeks, but the small completer-only sample, missing DXA observations, broad intervals and reduced bioavailability of the compounded preparation leave substantial uncertainty. No primary VAT benefit was demonstrated; this surrogate finding cannot establish lifespan extension or rule out an adiposity effect.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Pharmacy-managed randomization and matching capsules kept participants and study staff masked. Eleven randomized participants were excluded as noncompleters; endpoint-specific missingness used pairwise removal, and adherence was largely self-reported.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Visceral adiposity was the prespecified primary body-composition endpoint in normative aging, not a validated measure of lifespan extension. The compounded product and selected healthy cohort limit wider applicability.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The improvement odds-ratio intervals are broad: 0.73–4.50 at 5 mg and 0.66–4.32 at 10 mg. They do not exclude important differences; a nonsignificant test is not evidence of equivalence.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: This is one small three-arm trial, with both doses sharing one placebo group. Dose arms and secondary outcomes are not independent replications, and no pooled longevity estimate is justified.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: The hashed original PDF and its embedded tables and enrollment schematic were inspected locally; companion files were hash-verified. Authors disclosed AgelessRx employment/ownership and company support. This is local editorial inspection, not independent or human approval.

records.rationale: The reported between-group lean-tissue contrast favors 10 mg compounded rapamycin in women, but few women contributed, endpoint-specific observations were missing, and this was a secondary subgroup among many analyses. Confidence in a general clinical benefit is low despite the positive adjusted comparison; muscle function, sarcopenia treatment and longevity were not demonstrated.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Pharmacy-managed randomization and matching capsules kept participants and study staff masked. Eleven randomized participants were excluded as noncompleters; endpoint-specific missingness used pairwise removal, and adherence was largely self-reported. The reported pairwise contrast used a multiple-comparison correction, but sex-specific secondary analyses still require cautious interpretation.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The direct measurement is baseline-normalized lean tissue on DXA in women, not strength, walking performance, diagnosed sarcopenia or survival. It cannot be generalized to all older adults or other formulations.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The 48-week contrast is +6.194 percentage points with 95% CI 0.8773–11.5105. The wide range and small subgroup leave the size and practical significance uncertain; subgroup follow-up N is not fully reconciled here.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: A 24-week signal in the same participants is not independent replication. No significant male benefit or benefit across all doses is inferred, and the null primary VAT result remains separately visible.

records.rationale: Two controlled mouse cohorts and repeated imaging support an experimental bone finding, but small female-only groups, model-specific exposures and incomplete reporting of allocation concealment prevent a confident human clinical inference. The evidence is explicitly preclinical, with no human trial count, treatment effect or benefit letter.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Vehicle controls and two colonies strengthen the experiment; JAX imaging was longitudinal and image landmarking used randomized images and independent observers. Allocation concealment and complete investigator blinding were not established in this appraisal.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: These are aged female mouse periodontal-bone measurements, not clinical attachment, tooth retention or symptoms in patients. Dietary concentration cannot be translated into a human therapeutic dose.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: NIA-UW had 10 old mice per treatment and JAX 13 per treatment. Directional findings were reported with tests and plots; a numeric effect and interval were not extracted, so no magnitude is asserted.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: Concordant findings at two sites within one report improve experimental coherence but are not independent human replication. Different colonies and imaging designs remain separate.

records.rationale: The report links xenograft growth inhibition to TCF dependence using negative and rescue controls, but the findings arise from cell and immunodeficient-mouse models at nonclinical exposures. Small experiments, no human comparator and unresolved translation leave weak support for any clinical colorectal-cancer inference; no A–F clinical benefit grade is assigned.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Carrier controls, TCF-independent models and constitutively active TCF rescue test pathway specificity. The local report did not establish allocation concealment or blinded tumor measurements for this appraisal.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Human-derived cells implanted in nude mice remain nonclinical evidence. Daily intraperitoneal exposure is not an oral cancer regimen in patients, and pathway-sensitive lines are a selected subset.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: Tumor growth was assessed serially with small experiment-level groups. A common numeric effect and confidence interval were not extracted, and no patient denominator or clinical magnitude is available.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: TCF-dependent inhibition and rescue are internally coherent, while TCF-independent growth is a material negative result. Multiple assays within one report do not establish replicated clinical benefit.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: The existing full-text XML hash matched its local acquisition manifest and contained experimental methods and figure captions. Supplements/raw experimental datasets were not independently reanalyzed; no fresh integrity search or human approval is claimed.

records.rationale: The source reports smaller A549 xenografts after a short fenbendazole course, but the animal experiment and cell mechanisms cannot establish patient benefit. Unclear randomization/blinding, limited quantitative precision and absent human efficacy data leave low clinical confidence, and no clinical benefit letter or human trial count is assigned.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: The paper used control xenografts with measured tumor size/weight and supporting tissue assays. Random allocation and blinded assessment were not established; reported tests were Student’s t tests.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The outcome is growth of implanted A549 tumors in immunodeficient mice, not response or survival in people with NSCLC. The mouse regimen cannot supply a human dose or therapeutic recommendation.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The short 12-day experiment reports directional size and weight reductions. A reliable numeric contrast with interval was not extracted; there is no patient sample or clinical effect size.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: Cell-cycle, metabolic and xenograft assays within this report support an experimental hypothesis, not independent clinical replication. They cannot outweigh or resolve human liver-injury concerns.
